key_insight: Changing initialization masks can overcome decoding restrictions in compressed QAOA that persist at every finite circuit depth with all-plus initialization.
engineering_relevance: Classical mask selection offers a way to improve decoded solutions without increasing quantum circuit depth.
method: Prove an all-depth decoding obstruction for a fixed Pauli encoding on an infinite family of connected cubic graphs.
Show that random signed product-state masks yield a linear expected cut advantage at fixed depth-one angles.
Test classical mask selection before energy optimization using noiseless simulations.
evidence_signal: Across 1,699 random cubic MaxCut instances, one selected mask achieved a mean ratio of 0.9100, versus 0.7067 for the all-plus X baseline and 0.9125 for the best of r² separately optimized random masks.
watch_item: The simulations are noiseless, selected masks do not consistently beat the random-mask pool, and no quantum computational advantage is established.
paper_title: Initialization masks overcome decoding obstructions in compressed QAOA
